name: task-113-lazy-rerank-ab-intel-local
comment: Joint Task 112+113 lazy heap-f32 rerank A/B (supersedes reviews/task-112/001-.../artifacts/task-112-lazy-rerank-ab.intel-local.json). NON-STANDARD config (justified): the canonical lane sweep carries no heap-f32 coarse_rerank index nor a lazy on/off A/B. Two matched arms over one IVF heap-f32 index per scale (storage_format='coarse_rerank', rerank='heap_f32', rerank_format='f32', rerank_placement='table', rerank_width=64), driven by the per-step session_guc ec_ivf.lazy_heap_rerank = on|off. recall/latency steps use the standard ec_ivf nprobe default_sweep [8,16,24,32,48,64] verbatim. IMPORTANT STATUS: Task 113 wired RaBitQLazyBound::default() (slack=+inf == NoBound) as the live bound seam, but no skip fires yet because (a) min_kept == rerank_width (no k-cap / incremental cross-amgettuple emission) and (b) a tight sound f(approx) bound is unavailable from RaBitQ (its calibrated envelope is probabilistic, rejected as recall-risky). So this A/B is STILL EXPECTED to show byte-identical recall/ordering and EQUAL heap rerank rows / source bytes / latency between arms (rerank_candidates_skipped == 0). It exists to (a) confirm the gate stays recall-neutral on a real corpus with the new bound seam, and (b) become the live win measurement once the k-cap + per-candidate sound bound carriage land (the documented remaining Phase 4 levers). ENV-BLOCKED on this dev/review box. Run on the Intel bench desktop after staging ec_real_100k. Evidence Requirements per cell from results.jsonl: recall@10, NDCG@10, p50/p95/p99/mean, rerank_candidates_considered, rerank_candidates_skipped, rerank_rows (heap rerank rows), rerank_source_bytes_read.

steps.name: precheck-host
args: SELECT now() AS captured_at, version() AS postgres_version, current_setting('ec_ivf.lazy_heap_rerank') AS lazy_heap_rerank_default, current_setting('ec_ivf.posting_bound_prune') AS posting_bound_prune_default;
